items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I met a journalist named Edgar Higgins who wrote for the Chicago Defender under the name of the Street Wolf of Paris.

ctx.x: There was a bar downstairs in the hotel owned by Madame Liseux who was a beautiful amazon perhaps in her late 30s. I started to drink with some people in the bar and my voice was getting hoarser and hoarser. Finally someone persuaded me to go up to my room and get some rest, but it was 11 o'clock that night before I got to bed. I slept until 6 p.m. the next day and when I awakened, I had my voice back again.

The day after, we started rehearsing the show we had done in Monte Carlo with a French orchestra at the Rex theater. This was the largest theater I had ever seen or played in. There was plenty of space for the show at the Sporting d'Ete and it was the same at the Rex because the two bands were on the stage opposite each other and we still seemed to be a mile apart. There were quite a few American negros in Paris and many of them made the Hotel Liseux their meeting place. There was an American negro girl singer named Neeka Shaw who had a cabaret where a fine pianist by the name of Freddie Johnson was playing. I had heard some musicians in New York speak about Freddie Johnson and he was everything I had heard about him concerning his piano playing. Neeka's place was called the Hot Feet and was on Rue Pigalle 53.
